messages.author: 6123b161185c6a93
messages.subject: hurdle model predictions
parts:
Hello everyone!,

I have run a hurdle model that has a binomial and a gamma process.
My question is regarding the predictions for the gamma component when y = 0. I want to get predictions such as binomial_prediction * gamma_prediction.

However, the gamma_predictions when y=0 are super out of range, for example, 147629, while the 95th percentile of the response (y) is 9097.
I have also calculated the predictions by hand: intercept + slope1*var1 + slope2*var2 ... and I got lower predictions, eg, 727 instead of 147629. 
Also, when y > 0, the predictions yielded by INLA and the ones I obtain manually are pretty much the same.

So, I'm wondering how INLA produces predictions for the gamma component when the response is supposed to be zero. I know that a value of zero doesn't make sense for the gamma distribution, but I expected lower predictions...

Thank you very much in advance!
Juanmi

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] hurdle model predictions
parts:
hi & thanks for your email.

Have you accounted for the probability of zero and non-zero ? these are
not included in the predictions, like

p * 1{y=0} + (1-p) f(y)

f.ex. then the predictions does not include the (1-p) term.

let me know
H
